title: Time analyticity of bounded zero-observation semilinear skew-adjoint evolutions with compact analytic nonlinearity
source_title: Global propagation of analyticity and unique continuation for semilinear waves
author: Camille Laurent; Cristóbal Loyola
difficulty_reason: Ordinary holomorphic ODE theory cannot directly recover the unbounded skew-adjoint evolution from zero observation. The authors first build a uniform high-frequency observation inverse and propagate regularity with the complete commutator/resolvent argument, then construct the source-specific real and complex nonlinear reconstruction with uniform contraction and holomorphic parameter control. Their full time-translation and reconstruction argument reduces the remaining observed solution to a bounded Banach-space ODE, supplying the new finite-time analyticity obligation after the precise standard ODE and contraction prerequisites.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem1.8 in the bounded regime explicitly used in its proof: real separable Hilbert X, skew-adjoint A with compact-resolvent AstarA, fixed sigma>0, bounded observation C with observability over time T in both X^sigma and X^(sigma+epsilon), and exact commutator regularity Assumption4. F maps B_(4R0)(X^sigma) boundedly/Lipschitz into X^(sigma+epsilon) and has the uniformly bounded Lipschitz holomorphic extension of Assumption3. Tstar>T, analytic strip sources H1,H2 with exact real-part H1 bound, and solution U on[0,Tstar] with CU=0 and sup norm in X^sigma at most R0, as the proof physical29 explicitly uses. Then U is time analytic on(0,Tstar) in X^sigma. Full new uniform linear observation inversion17–19, regularity/commutator smoothing21–22, nonlinear reconstruction23–28 and translated Banach-ODE closure29–32 read. Authored Appendix A.1/A.2 ODE translation support59–60 read. Named holomorphic Banach Taylor/Cauchy/ODE and parameter contraction theorems are explicit published background. The bounded solution condition is retained from the proof, without extending a locally defined F to arbitrary trajectories. No specific wave/plate propagation, unique continuation or energy-observability outcome counted; later application cores unreviewed.
